explanation:
## What the grids are made of

Each input has two kinds of content:

1. **Structured shapes**: a connected multi-colour blob built mostly from one "structural" colour (3 in pair 1, 8 in pairs 2 and 3, 5 in the test), with a few single cells of other colours (1, 2, 4) embedded in it. For example in pair 1 the vertical 3‑shape has a 2 at its top, a 4 at its left and a 1 at its bottom.
2. **Scattered markers**: isolated single cells of exactly those same embedded colours (1, 2, 4), lying somewhere else in the grid in a different arrangement.

The structural colour is easy to identify: it is the most common non‑background colour. Every shape is a multi‑colour component that contains at least one cell of that colour; every other non‑background cell is a target marker.

## How the output is built

Comparing input and output, the original shape region is wiped to background, and the structural colour reappears around the scattered markers. In pair 3 the input shape is a horizontal bar `1 8 8 8 2 8` with an 8 above and below the 2 and a 4 above the 2; the scattered markers are 1 at (11,1), 2 at (11,5), 4 at (13,5). In the output the 8‑bar runs from the 1 to the 2 again, but the 4 is now *below* the 2, so the shape has been flipped vertically. Pair 2's shapes are rotated as well. So the rule is:

> Each shape, with its embedded marker colours, is rotated/reflected (one of the 8 symmetries) and translated so that its embedded markers land exactly on scattered markers of the same colours. The shape is redrawn there and erased from its original place.

The scattered markers act as a legend of "where the coloured pieces must end up", and the matching of colours fixes both orientation and position uniquely.

## Checking

I implemented this literally: for each shape, try all 8 orientations; for each one, align the first embedded marker with every scattered marker of its colour and check that all other embedded markers also land on scattered markers of the right colour. The first consistent match is used. Run on all three train pairs this reproduced every output cell for cell, with a unique match found for every shape.

## The test input

The test has structural colour 5 and two shapes: one around (3..6, 5..10) with markers 1, 4, 2, and one around (9..11, 10..13) with markers 2, 1, 4. There are two triples of scattered markers: (2 at (13,2), 4 at (13,4), 1 at (15,4)) and (4 at (16,10), 1 at (19,10), 2 at (21,12)). The first shape is rotated so its 2 goes to (13,2), 4 to (13,4) and 1 to (15,4); the second is rotated so 4→(16,10), 1→(19,10), 2→(21,12), with the 5‑structure drawn around them. The original shapes are erased.

The emit stages are: erase a shape, then stamp it in its new orientation at the target markers, for each shape in turn; then the final canvas.
